page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48-lssd is an ARM-based server instance featuring 48 dedicated physical cores powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz. It is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates without hyperthreading, allocating one thread per physical core.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and high memory throughput. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated in the top 25% with a score of 86659.83, while single-core performance remains in the middle 50% at 1821.19. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 334.84 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 158.43 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is exceptionally strong, reaching the top 10% tier at 532.16 GB/sec.

The combination of high memory density, dedicated ARM cores, and integrated local NVMe SSD storage provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require x86 instruction sets. The absence of AVX or AMX extensions represents a tradeoff for specific vector or matrix math workloads, but the hardware is well-suited for large-scale databases, memory-cached applications, multi-threaded data decompression, and high-throughput local storage operations.
